title: Payment Arrangements — Restructuring the Installment When Income Has Fallen
content:
## The rule in force

A consumer whose income has fallen may ask to lower the regular installment of an active plan by a restructure, which the consumer authorizes personally, stating the household income for the budget review where the type requires one. This applies to plans under Payment Arrangements.

The restructured installment is fixed only after the installment history carries a re-aging deferral for the installment with the most recent missed entry.

The restructured installment is not worked out before the installment history records as missed the last installment whose pre-suspension grace had run out by the time missed-installment counting stopped.

Both are conditions on what the installment history shows: without that re-aging deferral entry the restructured installment is not fixed, and without that missed entry it is not worked out.

When a re-aged installment stands behind the final installment, the restructured installments run from the schedule anchor date on the plan's frequency and the re-aged installment moves to one period after the last of them, so the plan's final due date after the restructure is the re-aged installment's new due date and the installment count after the restructure is the schedule anchor installment plus the restructured count; otherwise the final due date is the due date of the last restructured installment.

## What the authorization does

One restructure is recorded on the arrangement's installment history, starting with the arrangement's next due installment, and the arrangement is rewritten with the new regular installment amount, the new total number of installments, the new final due date, the consumer's stated net monthly household income for the budget review, today's date as the date of the consumer's authorization and the way it was given. The payment method and the next due date are not changed. Afterwards the consumer can see the new regular installment, the installment count and the final due date on the arrangement.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `authorize_restructured_installments_370d01b0`. It belongs to the consumer: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves — the consumer on the call — runs it to authorize the restructure personally.

## Parameters

- `plan_id` — the payment plan reference number (the identifier) of the consumer's arrangement, as read to the consumer by the agent from the arrangement record.
- `installment_amount` — the new regular installment amount, in USD, a decimal number rounded to 2 decimal places.
- `installment_count` — the new total number of installments of the arrangement, counting the installments already paid and any down payment, a positive integer.
- `final_due_date` — the due date of the last installment after the restructure, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- `stated_net_monthly_income` — the consumer's net monthly household income as the consumer states it for the budget review, in USD, a decimal number rounded to 2 decimal places.
- `authorization_method` — how the consumer gives this authorization, one of: `recorded_call` (the consumer authorizes on the recorded telephone call in progress); `e_signature` (the consumer signs the authorization electronically).

## Return

On success the tool returns a record rendered as text with `change_reference` (the reference of the restructure recorded), `plan_id`, `first_installment` (the first installment at the new amount), `installment_amount` (USD), `installment_count`, `final_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `authorization_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and `status`, always `restructure_authorized`, which shows the restructure is recorded.

When no arrangement matches the reference given, the tool returns "No payment plan found for" followed by that reference, and nothing is recorded.
